title: FUSE: Frequency-domain Unification and Spectral Energy Alignment for Multi-modal Object Re-Identification
claim: Prior methods fuse modalities with separate spatial-domain encoders; ours works in the frequency domain, splitting features into low, mid and high bands for richer fusion.
layout: 2 stacked panels (a) prior, (b) ours, left-to-right flow, dashed rounded boxes
description: Two stacked dashed-border panels contrast spatial and frequency approaches to multi-modal person re-identification. Panel (a), 'Current spatial-domain network', shows three stacked input images (RGB in red, near-infrared in green, thermal in blue) going into three separate colored Vision Transformer blocks. These produce blue, green and red feature cubes linked by curved gray 'Interaction' arrows. The result is a single 'spatial-domain' heat-map of the pedestrian. Panel (b), 'Our proposed FUSE', has the same three inputs going into one shared Vision Transformer. Its outputs are Fourier spectrum images marked with blue, orange and purple boxes for the low, mid and high bands. Pink 'Interaction' arrows connect the spectra. The final output is three heat-maps labeled Low, Mid and High, showing the person's silhouette, edges and fine texture. The eye goes first to the colorful pedestrian images and the red-to-blue contrast between the panels.
caption: Comparison between the proposed FUSE and mainstream spatial-domain structures. (a) Existing multi-modal ReID methods mainly rely on spatial domain fusion, but the inherent low-frequency bias [ref] of both CNNs and ViTs causes models to predominantly capture global low-frequency semantics while neglecting mid and high-frequency details, leading to incomplete spectral representation and unstable cross-modal alignment. (b) The proposed FUSE explicitly models in the frequency domain, where spectral decomposition and energy alignment partition features into low, mid, and high-frequency subspaces, achieving semantically interpretable cross-modal feature fusion.
abstract: Despite significant progress in multi-modal Re-Identification (ReID), existing methods tend to emphasize low-frequency cues. Consequently, they focus on attributes such as color, illumination, and coarse appearance, while overlooking mid and high-frequency structures that encode geometric, textural, and identity-discriminative details. This imbalance leads to incomplete spectral representations and unstable cross-modal alignment. To overcome these limitations, we introduce FUSE, a frequency-domain framework that reformulates multi-modal ReID as a two-stage process of spectral disentanglement and energy alignment. The proposed Spectral Decomposition Module (SDM) adaptively partitions features into low, mid, and high-frequency subspaces, enabling hierarchical spectral modeling. The Cross-Modal Alignment Module (CAM) further enforces energy alignment and subspace complementarity across modalities via frequency-consistency regularization. In addition, FUSE incorporates learnable frequency modulation to enhance robustness under varying illumination and heterogeneous sensor conditions. Extensive experiments on RGBNT201, RGBNT100, and MSVR310 show that FUSE achieves 9.1\% mAP and 9.5\% Rank-1 improvements, establishing an interpretable frequency-domain paradigm for multi-modal representation learning.
